seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The program's output is in `answer.txt`, and room rq1 accepted it unanimously (3 of 3 votes) before I left. I traced the program by hand against the spec rather than running an interpreter.

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

The other two seats first submitted 1027 and 1008 for the `outer` and `mid` results. That assumes `deep` can see `mid`'s parameter `b`, which is dynamic scoping. The spec's SCOPE rules say a read uses the call's own locals and otherwise the global, so `deep` reads the global `b` (2000). Both seats agreed after rechecking.

seats.name: seat-2
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3/3), and `answer.txt` contains the agreed answer. I checked it by tracing the program by hand against the spec. I didn't run any interpreter, and the `verify/seat2` board entry records that manual trace.

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

My first trace had `3007 3005` as `1027 1008`. I had let `deep` see `mid`'s parameter `b`, but each call has its own locals, so `deep` reads the global `b` (2000). seat-1's answer was right, and I switched to it before voting.

I have left the room.

seats.name: seat-3
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-3 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
I wrote the program's output to `answer.txt`, and room rq1 agreed on it 3 to 3. I traced the program by hand and did not run it.

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

My first trace had 1027 and 1008 in the 10th and 11th positions. seat-1 pointed out that `deep` is a separate call. It can't see `mid`'s parameter `b`, so it reads the global `b` (2000) instead of 20. That makes the 10th and 11th values 3007 and 3005, and I amended the proposal to match. seat-2 had made the same mistake and switched too.

I've left the room.
